source.title: Alignment Risks from Capability-Seeking RL Training
source.authors: Yu-Jun Zhou; Yue Huang; Han Bao; Ke-Han Guo; Zhen-Wen Liang; Pin-Yu Chen; Tian Gao; Werner Geyer; Nuno Moniz; Nitesh V. Chawla; Xiang-Liang Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses subliminal learning as a distinct, complementary mechanism, but does not test transmission through semantically unrelated, filtered outputs or any of the listed claim versions. Its SFT results concern students trained on examples that directly demonstrate exploit strategies.
record.gate_note: The SFT exploit-transfer results in Table 6 are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version: the training examples are successful exploit examples, not semantically unrelated outputs filtered to remove references to the trait. The paper does not test the same-base condition, hidden-signal mechanisms, or prompt-only transmission.
record.test_reason: The paper names subliminal learning (Cloud et al., 2025) once, as distinct from its own work. Its SFT 'distillation' trains students on explicit successful exploit examples, not on semantically unrelated, filtered outputs. None of versions A–F is tested; no same/different-base comparison, no hidden-signal mechanism, no prompt-only test.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SFT on exploit examples can propagate exploit behaviour, unevenly across tasks and models. They explicitly distinguish this from subliminal learning driven by hidden data artifacts.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses SFT on examples that explicitly show successful exploits generated by an RL-trained teacher, not filtered semantically unrelated outputs carrying a hidden signal.
record.method_sensitivity: SFT adoption varies across tasks and student models, as shown in Table 6.

fits_no_version.finding: SFT on successful exploit examples from an RL-trained teacher raised students' exploit rates in most task–model pairs (e.g. Llama ProxyM 0→99.9%, Qwen3-4B-Base RewT 0→93.2%). Adoption was uneven: Qwen3-4B ProxyM 0→4.0%, and Qwen3-4B-Base SelfG fell from 9.0% to 2.2%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning on examples that explicitly demonstrate an exploit propagates the exploit to students, unevenly across tasks and models.

record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the Table 6 values. The reported SFT transfer findings concern explicitly demonstrated exploit strategies, so they do not provide evidence for the filtered, semantically unrelated-output claim.
record.rows_left_out: Table 6 task-performance values were not extracted because the related finding concerns exploit adoption, not the claimed hidden-signal transmission. Table 7 correction results and other exploit-training results were not extracted because they do not bear on the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No teacher outputs that are semantically unrelated to the trait and filtered; the SFT data directly demonstrate the exploit.
No comparison of same- versus different-base teacher–student pairs for hidden-signal transfer.
No transmission of misalignment through unrelated, filtered data.
No analysis of what carries a hidden signal.
No full fine-tuning versus LoRA-rank or evaluation-prompt robustness tests of subliminal transfer.
No prompt-only insertion of linked tokens.

record.verdict_notes: The relation is changed from discusses to cites_only: subliminal learning appears only in one related-work sentence distinguishing the paper's scope. Table 6 values were checked: only r2's baseline was misread. r4 should be noted as having no exploit data to distil.

versions.untested_parts: No test of trait-bearing teacher outputs that are semantically unrelated and filtered to remove references to the trait.
No comparison of students with the same versus different base models as the teacher.
No test of misalignment or alignment-relevant traits transmitted through the filtered, semantically unrelated-output route.
No investigation of the signal mechanism named in this version.
No tests of full fine-tuning, LoRA ranks, or evaluation prompts differing from training prompts for the claimed route.
No prompt-only test inserting linked tokens without fine-tuning.

relation.reason: There is one sentence (Section 2) setting the work apart from subliminal learning 'driven by hidden data artifacts'. The paper does not discuss it further.

tranche.reason: Subliminal learning is named once, to contrast it with the paper's work. The SFT data shows the exploits explicitly; there are no semantically unrelated filtered outputs and no same/different-base test.

source_check.notes: Table 6 is flattened in the text, but its column order is confirmed by numbers in the prose (e.g. Llama ContC GRPO 72.8, Qwen3-4B-Base SelfG Ori 9.0). The text does not say whether each student's teacher is the same base model's GRPO checkpoint, although the table pairs them per model. The authors' conclusion paraphrase is correct.

statements.correction: Optional detail: Qwen3-4B-Base SelfG fell 9.0% -> 2.2% (teacher 81.6%); Qwen3-4B RewT stayed 0% (teacher also 0%).
statements.problem: none. Exploit rates rose in 10 of 12 task-model pairs; the cited numbers match Table 6.
